hero.intro: Matheus lived with courage, faith, humor, and deep love for family and friends. This space was created to honor his life, share his story, and hold the memories that continue to bloom because of him.

story.para1: Matheus was a fighter, a believer, a dreamer, and a relationship-builder. He lived each day with gratitude and courage, inspiring everyone around him with his kindness, strong faith, and unwavering determination.
story.para2: He cherished his family deeply, valued his friendships, and found joy in the simple moments that made life meaningful. His legacy lives on in the love he gave so freely and the lives he touched so profoundly.
story.para3: Those who knew him remember his warm humor, his steady faith, and his gift for making everyone feel like family. Whether he was behind the wheel of his beloved Jaguars and Range Rovers or resting under the oak trees at home, Matheus found beauty in every day he was given - and he shared it freely with everyone around him.
story.para4: Every year after his transplant was a gift, and Matheus lived like he knew it. He turned hospital rooms into places of laughter, setbacks into stories of hope, and strangers into lifelong friends. Through every battle, his courage showed the people around him what it means to keep fighting - and to keep loving - no matter what comes.
story.quote: He lived fully, loved deeply, and held onto hope through every impossible moment.
story.timelineTitle: Journey of Matheus’ Heart Transplant & Fighting Spirit
story.t2018Body: After developing heart complications in his mid-to-late 50s, Matheus suffered a silent heart attack and was hospitalized in June 2018 in critical condition. He underwent open-heart surgery, received an LVAD, and five months later received the gift of a 20-year-old donor heart.
story.t2018Strong: On July 22, 2018, he successfully received his heart transplant at UCSF.
story.t2024Body: In June 2024, while visiting family and friends in Los Angeles, he suffered acute heart transplant rejection. In the ICU, his heart stopped for 26 minutes, yet he survived. Still unconscious, he was airlifted back to UCSF, underwent weeks of intensive treatment, and recovered enough to return home.
story.t2026Body: Nearly eight years after his transplant, Matheus experienced severe kidney complications and was admitted to UC Davis Medical Center on June 11, 2026, then transferred to UCSF. After intensive treatment, he asked for one final wish: to return home, ride once more in his beloved Jaguars and Range Rovers, and spend his remaining days under the oak trees he loved, surrounded by family and close friends.
story.t2026Strong: On June 18, 2026, he made the journey home.
story.giftBody: Against all expectations, Matheus spent 18 more days at home surrounded by the people, places, and memories he cherished most. Those days were filled with love, laughter, visitors, favorite foods, and moments that became lifelong memories. In the end, perhaps his greatest miracle was being given the chance to spend his final days exactly where he wanted to be: at home,
